title: PROP-113 residual 23/day integrity resurrection: ROOT CAUSE is cross-bash-session loss of $GIT_DELETED_SET in smart_copy (PROP-066 class), NOT the Fix C tombstone-age window and NOT a producer-fresh shallow-clone blob fail-open. Fix = deterministic in-clone set path + fail-closed guard for prune-managed integrity + re-add-event Fix C v2.
executive_summary: PROP-113 Fix C added a post-sync resurrection assertion to workspace-sync.md that is supposed to make a resurrection-causing cycle self-evident on the run that caused it. It calls check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 2. That script filters candidates by TOMBSTONE mtime (check-prune-resurrection.js line 53: if(mt && mt < cutoff) continue), so --hours 2 only considers files tombstoned in the last 2 hours. The actual prune<->workspace-sync re-add loop re-adds files that were tombstoned DAYS ago: FUSE retains the per-run JSON indefinitely (no unlink), prune deletes the git copy, and a later workspace-sync re-adds it. The re-add EVENT is fresh but the TOMBSTONE is old. Result: Fix C reports resurrection_status='clean' on the exact run that re-added 17 tombstoned narrative-cite-audit files. The assertion provides false assurance — it is structurally incapable of catching the dominant loop shape. The 48h tinker-side canary catches it; the 2h self-assertion cannot.
root_cause: Window semantics mismatch. check-prune-resurrection.js windows by tombstoned_at (rec.mtime), not by re-add event time. Fix C narrowed the window to --hours 2 specifically to avoid re-flagging pre-existing residue every run ('a wider window re-flags pre-existing residue and would abort every run until backfill drains', workspace-sync.md ~line 1583). That reasoning is sound for a tombstone-age window but it throws out exactly the events Fix C exists to catch: a re-add today of a file tombstoned yesterday. Tombstone-age windowing and re-add-event detection are different questions; Fix C asks the wrong one.
other_side_Q4_ruled_out: Counter-argument: maybe --hours 2 is correct and the residual 23 are just pre-fix backlog that will drain once prune re-tombstones, so the assertion SHOULD ignore them. Rejected by evidence: commit 5a20dcd (2026-06-22T23:09:48Z, ~7h AFTER PROP-113 P3 deployed at 16:15) re-added 17 narrative-cite-audit files with git status 'A' (396,638 insertions), and the matching run report run-2026-06-22T23-10-45Z.json recorded resurrection_status='clean', git_deleted_set_untrusted=false, git_deleted_count=2589. That is a NEW re-add event post-deploy, not static backlog, and Fix C declared it clean. A correct assertion must flag the run that performs the re-add regardless of how old the tombstone is. Secondary counter-argument: widening to --hours 48 in the assertion would make it abort almost every run (because residue persists), turning the abort sentinel into noise. Also rejected: the right detector is not a wider tombstone window but a re-add-event check (did THIS push add any path in the tombstone set), which only fires on actual re-adds and is silent on untouched residue.

evidence.canary_48h: check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 48 => RC=3, resurrected_total=23, all category narrative-cite-audit-archive.jsonl (tinker run 2026-06-23T02-40).
evidence.fixc_window_source: workspace-sync.md ~line 1589: RESURRECTION_OUT=$(node monitor/scripts/check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 2 ...). Comment at ~1583 documents the deliberate 2h narrowing.
evidence.script_filter: check-prune-resurrection.js line 41 cutoff=Date.now()-WINDOW_H*3600*1000; line 53 if(mt && mt < cutoff) continue; — mt is rec.mtime (tombstone time).
evidence.matching_readd_commit: 5a20dcd01561abab5b9a1716039e8b1b406ff57a 2026-06-22T23:09:48Z 'Workspace sync': 17 narrative-cite-audit-*.json added (status A) + 1 genuinely-new live file; tombstones for the 17 dated 2026-06-21T08:06 and 2026-06-22T08:05 (15-39h before the re-add).
evidence.depth50_repro: In a depth-50 clone, smart_copy's PROP-094 producer-fresh guard correctly SKIPs all 17 (pre-deletion blob sha1 == HEAD blob == FUSE src for each), so the re-add mechanism itself is shallow-clone-depth-sensitive in workspace-sync's runtime environment and is NOT reproducible at depth 50 — see complementary_work.

proposed_fix.summary: Replace the tombstone-age window in Fix C with re-add-event detection. After the push, compute the set of paths ADDED by this run's HEAD commit (git show --diff-filter=A --name-only HEAD) and intersect with the GIT_DELETED_SET already built this cycle (archive-tombstone-derived, depth-independent, available as $GIT_DELETED_SET). Any non-empty intersection => this run re-added a tombstoned path => write the abort/warning sentinel and set resurrection_status='ABORT-resurrection-detected'. This fires only on actual re-adds, is silent on untouched residue, and is independent of tombstone age and clone depth.
proposed_fix.concrete:
In workspace-sync.md Fix C block (~lines 1582-1611): after PUSH, run: ADDED=$(git show --diff-filter=A --name-only --pretty=format: HEAD | grep '^monitor/integrity/' || true); RESURRECTED=$(comm -12 <(printf '%s
' "$ADDED" | sort -u) <(sort -u "$GIT_DELETED_SET")); if [ -n "$RESURRECTED" ]; then resurrection_status=ABORT, write sentinel listing $RESURRECTED. Keep the check-prune-resurrection.js call as a SECONDARY signal if desired, but the primary gate must be the commit-add intersection.
proposed_fix.why_this_is_correct: GIT_DELETED_SET is exactly the set of prune-tombstoned paths workspace-sync must never re-add. If this run's commit added any member of that set, that is by definition a resurrection — no time window needed.

backfill_plan: None required for detection. The 23 currently-resurrected files remain until the next prune cycle re-tombstones them or the operator tree-deletes via the Git Data API escape hatch (CLAUDE.md). PROP-114 only fixes the DETECTION gap so future re-adds are caught on the causing run. The separate re-add MECHANISM (why smart_copy re-adds at all in workspace-sync's shallow clone despite the depth-50 guard passing) is tracked under complementary_work and likely needs the producer-fresh exception to fail-closed when last_del_sha or the pre-deletion blob is unresolvable in a shallow clone.
detection_mechanism: After fix: any run that re-adds a tombstoned integrity artifact writes monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-<ts>.json AND sets resurrection_status='ABORT-resurrection-detected' in its run report, on the SAME run. Verify by replaying against commit 5a20dcd: the commit-add intersection must be non-empty (17 paths).
complementary_work: PROP-099 (canary, pending) detects the loop after the fact at 48h — keep. This PROP makes workspace-sync self-report the causing run. The remaining open question — why the smart_copy PROP-094 producer-fresh guard re-adds in workspace-sync's runtime when a depth-50 clone correctly SKIPs — is a separate MECHANISM defect (likely the git log --diff-filter=D / git show parent-blob lookup behaving differently at workspace-sync's shallow clone depth). Recommend a follow-on PROP making the producer-fresh exception fail-closed (SKIP) when last_del_sha is found but the pre-deletion blob cannot be resolved, rather than the current behaviour which can RESCUE on an unresolvable/ambiguous comparison.
constraints_honored: Propose-only: no edits applied to workspace-sync.md this run.
Evidence-based: every claim cites a file, line, commit, or run report.

verification_pattern.pattern: Post-deploy of P2 (Diffs A+B+C): (1) SMOKE-3 + SMOKE-5 pass (fail-closed guard skips when set unavailable; no false positive on clean runs). (2) Across 2 consecutive days, every workspace-sync run report whose commit ADDED a tombstoned integrity path has resurrection_status='ABORT-resurrection-detected' (no more false 'clean') AND such commits trend to zero as prevention takes hold. (3) Loop-closed signal: check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 48 RC=0 sustained 2 days (the criterion transferred from PROP-113). (4) workspace-sync-skips.jsonl shows 'PROP-094 git-deleted-authoritative' SKIPs continuing for tombstoned paths (set reliably available) and/or 'PROP-114 fail-closed' SKIPs on any split run — but NO new narrative-cite re-add commits.
verification_pattern.note: Requires operator to ship P2 first; gated by requires_human_judgment=true.

mechanism_correction.note: The ORIGINAL PROP-114 (authored by tinker run 02-40) diagnosed two things: (1) Fix C's --hours 2 tombstone-age window is blind to the dominant loop shape [CORRECT — kept], and (2) the re-add MECHANISM is the PROP-094 producer-fresh exception fail-opening in workspace-sync's shallow clone because git show ${last_del_sha}^:dst behaves differently at depth [REFUTED by this amendment]. The directive (DIRECTIVE-20260623-001) asked for the root-cause detective work. It was done; the producer-fresh-blob hypothesis is empirically false. The actual root cause is ephemeral $GIT_DELETED_SET loss across MCP bash-tool-call boundaries (the PROP-066 cross-bash-session state-loss class).
mechanism_correction.original_complementary_work_field_was_wr: The original 'complementary_work' said the open question was 'why the smart_copy PROP-094 producer-fresh guard re-adds in workspace-sync's runtime when a depth-50 clone correctly SKIPs'. Answer: it does NOT re-add via the producer-fresh guard at all. A faithful depth-50 clone pinned at the runtime HEAD (5a20dcd^) computes the guard as SKIP (correct). The re-add happens because the guard is never reached: grep -qFx against an EMPTY $GIT_DELETED_SET matches nothing, so the whole PROP-094 block is skipped and the file falls through to cp.

Q1_Q2_root_cause_investigation.smoking_gun: On 2026-06-22, the path monitor/integrity/narrative-cite-audit-2026-06-20T0009Z.json was correctly SKIPped via PROP-094 deletion-authority at the 09:08, 11:09, and 21:12 workspace-sync runs (proven by workspace-sync-skips.jsonl entries with reason 'PROP-094 git-deleted-authoritative'), then RE-ADDED (git status A) at the 23:09 run (commit 5a20dcd). The file content never changed (FUSE sha1 51ad31be == re-added HEAD blob 51ad31be). So a content-identical, already-tombstoned file flipped from SKIP to re-add between 21:12 and 23:09.
Q1_Q2_root_cause_investigation.faithful_depth50_reproduction: A real depth-50 shallow clone pinned at the runtime pre-push HEAD (5a20dcd^ = 80d3f2dc) was fetched. In it: (a) build-git-deleted-set.js emits 2589 paths — EXACTLY matching the run report's git_deleted_count=2589 — and 0009Z IS in that set; (b) the PROP-094 producer-fresh guard computes last_del_sha=1af8525 (deletion at depth ~28), its parent blob IS present (depth ~29), last_blob_hash=51ad31be == fuse_hash=51ad31be, so the guard decision is SKIP (correct). Therefore the producer-fresh exception did NOT and could NOT have re-added 0009Z. The prior shallow-clone-blob-fail-open hypothesis is refuted.
Q1_Q2_root_cause_investigation.actual_mechanism: The re-add path is sync_glob 'monitor/integrity' '*.json' -> smart_copy. In smart_copy's dst-absent branch, the first gate is `if grep -qFx "$dst" "$GIT_DELETED_SET"`. $GIT_DELETED_SET is a /tmp file path held ONLY in a shell variable (workspace-sync.md line 734: GIT_DELETED_SET="/tmp/git-deleted-set-$$-${RANDOM}.txt"; it is NOT exported — line 788 exports only GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED/_COUNT/_LINES). The GIT_DELETED_SET build (lines 711-790) and the smart_copy loop (lines 790-960) sit in one ~600-line fenced bash block (Step 2, closes line 1005). When the workspace-sync agent (Sonnet) executes that block across MORE THAN ONE MCP bash-tool call — the documented PROP-066 split behavior (each bash tool call is a fresh shell, no env carryover) — the smart_copy loop's shell has $GIT_DELETED_SET EMPTY. `grep -qFx "$dst" ""` matches nothing (grep errors on empty filename, returns non-zero), so the PROP-094 block is skipped entirely; $GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED is also empty so PROP-103 fail-closed defaults to 0 (no skip); is_prune_expired returns false for the freshly-pruned 1-2-day-old batch (14-day window); the file falls through to `cp` and is resurrected.
Q1_Q2_root_cause_investigation.empirical_confirmation_of_mechanism: Simulated smart_copy's dst-absent branch for 0009Z with GIT_DELETED_SET='' (the cross-call-loss state): grep matched nothing, PROP-103 did not fire, is_prune_expired returned false, RESULT = cp (resurrected). With GIT_DELETED_SET=/tmp/runtime_set.txt (the real 2589-path set): grep matched -> PROP-094 -> producer-fresh -> SKIP (no re-add). The single variable being empty vs populated flips the outcome, exactly reproducing the SKIP@21:12 -> re-add@23:09 transition (21:12 ran Step 2 in one bash call; 23:09 split it).
Q1_Q2_root_cause_investigation.why_intermittent_23_per_day: Only the FRESHLY-pruned batch is eligible to resurrect on a lossy run: those files are currently absent in git (deleted by that day's prune) AND still inside the 14-day is_prune_expired window. Files pruned on earlier days were already re-added on a prior lossy cycle and are now present in git (dst exists -> mtime-guard no-op, not re-added). Files older than 14 days are caught by the is_prune_expired fallback even when the set is lost. So each lossy run resurrects ~one daily prune batch (~15-23 files), matching the observed 23/48h. The 8290 'PROP-094 git-deleted-authoritative' SKIP records in workspace-sync-skips.jsonl prove the set IS usually available — the loss is intermittent, firing only on runs where the agent split Step 2.
Q1_Q2_root_cause_investigation.secondary_observability_gap: The 23:10 run report claims skips_total=625 but persisted ZERO records to workspace-sync-skips.jsonl (grep for that run_id / any 2026-06-22T23 timestamp returns nothing). This is the SAME disease on a second ephemeral variable: $SKIP_LOG (an mktemp path, also not surviving cross-call) was empty/unreadable in the Step-4b persist call, so the run's skip detail — including any evidence of the re-adds — was silently dropped. This is why the resurrection was invisible in the structured skip log and only the 48h tinker canary caught it.

hypothesis_ranking.best_fit: (i) — 'Fix A never trips because the set is honest; Fix B's helper is correct but smart_copy has a SEPARATE GAP.' Confirmed. The helper is correct (2589 paths incl. 0009Z). The separate gap is that smart_copy cannot SEE the set when $GIT_DELETED_SET is lost across a bash-call split. Precise mechanism is the PROP-066 ephemeral-state-loss class — a refinement of (i) not explicitly enumerated in the directive.
hypothesis_ranking.partially_right: (iii) — 'a code path that doesn't consult GIT_DELETED_SET.' In EFFECT correct: the consult runs but against an empty path, so it is as if the set is never consulted. Same smart_copy code path, lost state.
hypothesis_ranking.right_family_wrong_specific: (iv) — 'FUSE->git race: file committed before GIT_DELETED_SET sees latest archive append.' Wrong specific (the set DID contain the records; the archive tombstones were committed days earlier in b24f419/1af8525), but the right FAMILY — a state/timing problem, not a logic-threshold problem.
ruled_out: (ii) Fix A misconfigured — RULED OUT: set is honest (2589 < archive_lines 21274), Fix A's upper-bound gate correctly did not trip; Fix A is irrelevant to this failure mode.

(v) NEVER_PUSH-strand / universal-pusher path — RULED OUT: narrative-cite-audit is a standard prune-managed integrity artifact synced via sync_glob->smart_copy, not a NEVER_PUSH or runtime-data rescue path.

Q1_Q2_root_cause_investigation.what_run_report_alone_cannot_rule_out: The run report fields (git_deleted_count=2589, git_deleted_set_untrusted=false, resurrection_status='clean') are consistent with BOTH the (refuted) producer-fresh-blob-fail-open hypothesis AND the (confirmed) ephemeral-set-loss hypothesis — because the report is written by a DIFFERENT sub-step that DID see the exported _COUNT/_UNTRUSTED/_LINES vars while the smart_copy loop did not see $GIT_DELETED_SET. Distinguishing them required (a) the faithful depth-50 reproduction to refute the blob hypothesis and (b) the empty-variable simulation to confirm the ephemeral-loss hypothesis. Neither could be settled from the run report alone.

Q3_Q4_concrete_fix.design_decision: Q3 picks candidate (a): compare THIS run's commit-added paths against a freshly-built GIT_DELETED_SET. No new helper script required (Q4 = reuse existing build-git-deleted-set.js). BUT visibility (Fix C v2) alone does not stop the leak — it is post-commit and only detects. The load-bearing fix is the ROOT-CAUSE PREVENTION (Diffs A+B): make $GIT_DELETED_SET reconstructable from a deterministic in-clone path and fail-closed when it is still unavailable for prune-managed integrity. With prevention in place, Fix C v2 becomes a same-run canary that should report clean.

diff_A_deterministic_set_path.rationale: Replace the per-shell-random /tmp path with a deterministic in-clone path so a smart_copy loop running in a SEPARATE bash-tool call can still locate the set the build step wrote (the clone dir + .git persist across bash calls in the same session; only shell variables are lost). .git/ contents are never tracked, so no risk of committing the set.
diff_A_deterministic_set_path.new_string: GIT_DELETED_SET="$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null || echo .git)/dome-git-deleted-set.txt"   # PROP-114: deterministic in-clone path (survives bash-tool-call splits; .git is never tracked)

diff_A2_export_optional.note: Optional belt-and-suspenders: add GIT_DELETED_SET to the export list so in-call subprocesses see it. Does NOT help across bash-tool calls (export dies with the shell) — the deterministic path in Diff A + the default in Diff B are what actually close the cross-call gap. Include only if the operator wants the var visible to any in-call node helpers.

diff_B_failclosed_guard.rationale: In smart_copy's dst-absent branch, BEFORE the `grep -qFx` gate: (1) default $GIT_DELETED_SET to the deterministic in-clone path if the variable was lost across a bash-call split; (2) if the set is STILL unavailable (missing/empty), fail CLOSED for prune-managed integrity categories — we cannot prove the path is not a tombstoned artifact, so do not resurrect. Skipping is harmless (re-tries next cycle); resurrection is the disaster shape. This is the minimal, PROP-051-disaster-safe change — it can only REDUCE pushes, never mass-delete.
diff_B_failclosed_guard.old_string:
if grep -qFx "$dst" "$GIT_DELETED_SET" 2>/dev/null; then
      local last_del_sha last_blob_hash fuse_hash
diff_B_failclosed_guard.new_string:
# PROP-114 (2026-06-23): self-heal the deletion-authority set path. The Step 2
    # build (line ~734) and this smart_copy loop sit in one ~600-line fenced block;
    # when the agent runs them in SEPARATE bash-tool calls (PROP-066 cross-call state
    # loss) $GIT_DELETED_SET is EMPTY here, grep -qFx matches nothing, and the
    # freshly-pruned integrity batch falls through to cp -> resurrection (root cause
    # of the 2026-06-22 23/day leak; see PROP-114 Q1/Q2). Reconstruct the deterministic
    # in-clone path so a split loop still finds the set the build step wrote.
    : "${GIT_DELETED_SET:=$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null || echo .git)/dome-git-deleted-set.txt}"
    # Fail-closed backstop: if the set is STILL unavailable, do not resurrect
    # prune-managed integrity artifacts (harmless skip; opposite is the disaster).
    if [ ! -s "$GIT_DELETED_SET" ]; then
      case "$dst" in
        monitor/integrity/verify-pending-run-*.json|\
        monitor/integrity/narrative-cite-audit-*.json|\
        monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-runs/run-*.json|\
        monitor/integrity/push-failure-*.json|\
        monitor/integrity/report-*.json|\
        monitor/integrity/git-to-fuse-divergence-*.json|\
        monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-*.json)
          echo "SKIP (PROP-114 fail-closed; GIT_DELETED_SET unavailable, cannot verify deletion-authority): $dst" >> "$SKIP_LOG"
          return 0
          ;;
      esac
    fi
    if grep -qFx "$dst" "$GIT_DELETED_SET" 2>/dev/null; then
      local last_del_sha last_blob_hash fuse_hash
diff_B_failclosed_guard.validation: old_string matches workspace-sync.md @ commit 4c76b43 lines 604-605 verbatim (verified this run).

diff_C_fixc_v2_readd_event.rationale: Replace PROP-113 Fix C (check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 2, tombstone-age-windowed, blind to days-old re-adds) with re-add-event detection: rebuild the set HERE (deterministic in-clone path, independent of the Step-2 loop's shell state) and intersect with the paths THIS run's commit ADDED. Fires only on genuine re-adds, silent on untouched residue, independent of tombstone age and clone depth.

# Rebuild the deletion-authority set here so this assertion does not depend on the
# Step-2 $GIT_DELETED_SET surviving a bash-call split. Intersect with the paths THIS
# run committed as ADDED. Tombstone-age-independent; catches the days-old re-add the

gate:"PROP-114 Fix C v2 re-add-event detection",

reason:"workspace-sync commit ADDED prune-tombstoned integrity artifact(s) this cycle. Root-cause class: GIT_DELETED_SET unavailable in smart_copy shell (PROP-114). Verify the fail-closed guard + deterministic-set-path fix are deployed.",

diff_C_fixc_v2_readd_event.post_commit_visibility_note: Like PROP-113 Fix C, this runs AFTER the data commit+push, so it has NO abort authority over the data commit (honors the directive constraint + PROP-051 disaster sensitivity). Same-run visibility is achieved via resurrection_status='ABORT-resurrection-detected' in the run report (already pushed at end of run) plus the git-added sentinel (picked up next cycle). The operator may optionally add a tiny dedicated commit+push for the sentinel for instant visibility, but that adds a push and is not required.
diff_C_fixc_v2_readd_event.validation_evidence: Replayed against the real resurrection commit 5a20dcd in a depth-402 clone: build-git-deleted-set.js -> 2589 paths; git show --diff-filter=A 5a20dcd -> 17 integrity paths; intersection = 15 (the tombstoned re-adds), correctly EXCLUDING the 2 genuinely-new 2026-06-22 files. The OLD Fix C (--hours 2) reported resurrection_status='clean' for this exact commit. Proven improvement.

Q3_Q4_concrete_fix.Q4_helper_changes: None. Q3 picks candidate (a), which reuses the existing monitor/scripts/build-git-deleted-set.js unchanged. No new or modified helper script. (Candidate (b) — a --by-add-event mode on check-prune-resurrection.js — was considered and rejected: it duplicates the set-build the prevention fix already performs and adds a second source of truth.)

Q5_smoke_test.discipline: PROP-051-grade; mirrors PROP-113 amendment (reproduce false-clean, verify the fix catches it, verify a known-good cycle still passes, plus parity).
cases: SMOKE-1 (reproduce the false-clean / leak): in a real depth-50 clone pinned at runtime HEAD 5a20dcd^, simulate the cross-call state loss (GIT_DELETED_SET='') and run the dst-absent branch for a days-old tombstoned narrative-cite file present in FUSE. EXPECT current code -> cp (resurrect). EXECUTED THIS RUN: confirmed cp (resurrect).

Q5_smoke_test.executed_this_run: SMOKE-1, SMOKE-2, SMOKE-4 executed and PASSED during the Q1/Q2 investigation (see Q1_Q2 evidence). SMOKE-3 and SMOKE-5 are post-deploy validations (cannot run without applying the diffs, which is out of scope per propose-only).

Q6_disaster_vector_analysis.fixC_v2_abort_authority: NONE over the data commit. Fix C v2 runs post-commit/post-push; it only writes a sentinel and sets resurrection_status in the run report. Confirmed it cannot abort or roll back the data commit. Honors the directive constraint and PROP-051.
Q6_disaster_vector_analysis.failclosed_guard_effect_on_commit: The Diff-B fail-closed guard DOES affect the data commit — it skips (does not cp) a prune-managed integrity file when the set is unavailable. This is fail-CLOSED (fewer files pushed), the safe direction on the PROP-051 disaster axis: it can only REDUCE the push set, never trigger a mass-delete. Worst case if it false-positives (set legitimately unavailable on a run with a genuinely-new integrity file): that file is deferred ONE cycle and pushed next run when the set is available — loud (the SKIP reason floods the log) and self-correcting.
Q6_disaster_vector_analysis.sentinel_flood_bound: At most ONE resurrection-abort sentinel per run (a single file listing all detected paths, capped at 200 in resurrected_paths). Cannot flood integrity. Contrast with the resurrection itself, which adds ~15-23 multi-MB files/run.
Q6_disaster_vector_analysis.universal_pusher_interaction: The fail-closed guard is scoped by an explicit case-list to the 7 prune-managed integrity categories ONLY. Runtime data files (data/wins.json, open-issues.json, priority-queue.json, etc.) and the universal-pusher rescue path are entirely unaffected — they never match the case-list, so their dst-absent rescue behavior is unchanged.
Q6_disaster_vector_analysis.worst_case_perpetual_loss: If EVERY run split Step 2 (perpetual cross-call loss) AND the deterministic-path default somehow also failed, genuinely-new integrity artifacts would never sync — but that state is loud (every run logs the fail-closed SKIP reason) and far preferable to silent resurrection. The deterministic in-clone path (Diff A) makes this scenario very unlikely because the build step's output persists in the clone's .git across bash-tool calls within the same session.
Q6_disaster_vector_analysis.rollback: All three diffs are additive/local to workspace-sync.md (a NEVER_PUSH source file pushed only via build.js publish / operator).
